name: Phenytoin
summary: A classic sodium-channel-blocking anticonvulsant still used for focal and tonic-clonic seizures and status epilepticus, governed by nonlinear kinetics and heavy drug interactions.
mechanism: Use-dependent blockade of voltage-gated sodium channels, limiting high-frequency repetitive neuronal firing.

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: ~22 h at therapeutic concentrations (range 7–42 h; saturable)
pharmacokinetics.proteinBinding: ~90% (free fraction rises with hypoalbuminemia and renal failure)
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (CYP2C9/2C19); saturable (zero-order) kinetics at therapeutic concentrations

dosing.adult: Load 15–20 mg/kg IV or PO; maintenance 300–400 mg/day (5–6 mg/kg/day), titrated to total levels of 10–20 mg/L
dosing.renalAdjustment: Monitor free phenytoin in renal disease or hypoalbuminemia — total levels mislead

safety.pregnancy: Teratogen — fetal hydantoin syndrome (cleft lip/palate, cardiac defects, dysmorphism); avoid when possible
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to phenytoin or other hydantoins
Sinus bradycardia or AV block (IV administration)
warnings: SJS/TEN and DRESS — stop for unexplained rash
Narrow therapeutic index with nonlinear kinetics — small dose increases cause disproportionate level jumps
Gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, and folate deficiency with long-term use
Cardiac arrhythmias and hypotension with rapid IV infusion; purple glove syndrome with IV extravasation
Chronic toxicity — nystagmus, ataxia, cerebellar atrophy; monitor levels
monitoring: Total and free phenytoin levels (target total 10–20 mg/L)
safety.overdose: Nystagmus, ataxia, lethargy progressing to coma, and paradoxical seizures; supportive care — not significantly removed by hemodialysis

clinicalPearls: Zero-order kinetics: near the therapeutic ceiling, tiny dose increases cause large level jumps — titrate cautiously with levels
Free-level monitoring is essential in renal failure or hypoalbuminemia, where total levels overstate the active drug
good: Status epilepticus and established focal/GTC epilepsy when IV loading and level-guided dosing are available.
bad: Patients needing predictable kinetics or taking many interacting drugs — nonlinear clearance makes it unforgiving.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
